messages:
taylor: Heads up: found a weird edge where generator streams ignore ctx cancellation if you cancel during the initial handshake. Repro in minimal sampleapp.
sana: Oof. Does this only happen on fast cancels?
taylor: Yeah, if cancel happens <~20ms after Stream() returns. The recv loop blocks waiting for the pipe read.
luke: Can you paste the repro?
taylor: Minimal snippet:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
st, _ := client.Generator.Stream(ctx, req)
go func(){ time.Sleep(5 * time.Millisecond); cancel() }()
for {
  seg, err := st.Recv()
  if err != nil { break }
  fmt.Println(seg.Text)
}
```
The goroutine never exits on my machine, and we leak.
ram: Sounds similar to other cancel races we've seen. Is the connection using net/http Read? That won't unstick on ctx.Done unless we close the underlying transport.
sana: For sampleapps we can change examples to call stream.Close() after cancelling the ctx as a workaround. But we should fix the SDK behavior.
taylor: Agreed. Proposal: make Recv check ctx.Done at top of loop and return a context.Canceled error. Also ensure underlying reader is closed on cancel.
luke: Implementation note: need to avoid double-closing the transport if Recv caller also calls Close(). Might add an internal once.Do.
ram: Also add a boolean option in GeneratorOptions: InterruptOnCancel bool so it's opt-in for now. We can flip in v1.1.0.
sana: I'll update the quickstart in the repo to avoid immediate cancellation until this is resolved. New users hitting this will file confusing bug reports.
taylor: I'll open a small failing test in sampleapp that cancels during handshake and asserts goroutine count doesn't increase. PR -> https://go.redwood/pr/1256
devex-bot: Created issue INF-349 for generator stream cancellation + leak -> https://go.redwood/issue/INF-349
luke: Assigning to @ram to prototype. ETA: Thu.
ram: I'll prototype an Abort() on the stream and a ctx-aware Recv. Will post draft by EOD.
sana: Thanks — let's track in the SDK board and make sure release notes mention the behavior change.
